title_en: Lanzhou Zhenglin Agricultural Reclamation Food Co., Ltd. v. Lin Bojun and Zhengzhou Zhenglin Food Co., Ltd. — dispute over debt (retrial)
ruling_gist_en: Under the circumstances where a third party can resolve its creditor-debtor relationship with one party to the case by filing a separate lawsuit, and the parties to the case have reached a mediation agreement under the auspices of the people's court, and the mediation document issued by the people's court does not involve the creditor-debtor relationship between the third party and one party to the case, if the third party applies for a retrial of the mediation document issued by the people's court, such application does not comply with the provisions of Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China to the Trial Supervision Procedure regarding the filing of an application for retrial by a person not party to the case, and should be dismissed.
keywords_en: civil; debt dispute; retrial; Supreme People's Court; Henan Province; Gansu Province; natural person; legal person; Civil Procedure Law; qualification of a third party to apply for retrial; whether the mediation document infringes upon the interests of a third party; dismissal of claims; assignment of creditor's rights; mediation agreement; application for retrial by a third party; application for retrial; debt dispute of Zhenglin Food Co., Ltd.
full_text_en:
Lanzhou Zhenglin Agricultural & Food Co., Ltd. v. Lin Bojun and Zhengzhou Zhenglin Food Co., Ltd. — retrial of debt dispute

Ruling Summary

Where an outsider to the case may resolve its creditor-debtor relationship with one party to the case by filing a separate lawsuit, and where the parties to the case have reached a mediation agreement under the auspices of the people's court, and the mediation document issued by the people's court does not involve the creditor-debtor relationship between the outsider and the party to the case, an application for retrial of the mediation document filed by the outsider does not satisfy the provisions of Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 5 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China in the Trial Supervision Procedure regarding an outsider's initiation of retrial proceedings, and shall be dismissed.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Ruling
(2010) Min Shen Zi No. 1276

Retrial Applicant: Lanzhou Zhenglin Agricultural & Food Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 211, Yancang Road, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City, Gansu Province, People's Republic of China.
Legal Representative: Guo Yaopeng, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Chu Ningyu, lawyer at Shanghai Ding Ji Tie Law Firm.

Retrial Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Lin Bojun (PAI CHUN LIN BROWN), female, citizen of the United States of America, born on April 17, 1950. Domicile: State of California, United States of America. Passport No.: 434631075.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Qihan, lawyer at Beijing Gaojie Law Firm.

Retrial Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Zhengzhou Zhenglin Food Co., Ltd. Domicile: Yugang Avenue, Xinzheng Port Area, Zhengzhou City, Henan Province, People's Republic of China.
Legal Representative: Lin Ken, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Qihan, lawyer at Beijing Gaojie Law Firm.

The retrial applicant Lanzhou Zhenglin Agricultural & Food Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lanzhou Zhenglin), due to a dispute over debts with the retrial respondents Lin Bojun and Zhengzhou Zhenglin Food Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhengzhou Zhenglin), refuses to accept the Civil Mediation Document (2008) Yu Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 2 issued by the Henan High People's Court on November 14, 2008, and files an application for retrial with this Court. This Court has formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review this case, and the review is now concluded.

Lin Bojun, due to a debt dispute with Zhengzhou Zhenglin, filed a lawsuit with the Henan High People's Court on October 6, 2008, requesting the court to: 1. confirm that the "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement" signed by Lin Bojun, Zhengzhou Zhenglin, and Lanzhou Zhenglin on July 31, 2008, is lawful and valid; 2. order the defendant Zhengzhou Zhenglin to immediately repay the plaintiff Lin Bojun the outstanding amount of RMB 99,406,235.82 in accordance with the terms of the "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement"; 3. order the defendant to bear the litigation costs.

Upon the application of the parties, the Henan High People's Court presided over a mediation on November 14, 2008. The parties voluntarily reached the following mediation agreement through consultation: 1. Both parties confirm that as of July 16, 2008, Zhengzhou Zhenglin owed Lin Bojun RMB 99,406,235.82 which had not been repaid and had exceeded the agreed repayment period. 2. Due to Zhengzhou Zhenglin's financial and operational difficulties and inability to repay the above debt in cash to Lin Bojun within the agreed period, Zhengzhou Zhenglin voluntarily agrees to convert the entire debt owed to Lin Bojun into equity in Zhengzhou Zhenglin, based on the assessed value of all assets of Zhengzhou Zhenglin as of July 31, 2008. From the date of completion of the legal procedures for the change of equity registration, Lin Bojun shall become a shareholder of Zhengzhou Zhenglin, shall no longer enjoy the rights of a creditor, and shall instead enjoy the rights of a shareholder of Zhengzhou Zhenglin. Lin Bojun agrees to realize the satisfaction of the debt through debt-to-equity conversion. 3. Upon completion of the debt-to-equity conversion, the shares of Zhengzhou Zhenglin held by Lin Bojun shall be the percentage represented by the amount of Lin Bojun's debt as against the assessed value of all assets of Zhengzhou Zhenglin on the base date. 4. The legal procedures for the debt-to-equity conversion and the increase in registered capital of Zhengzhou Zhenglin due to the debt-to-equity conversion shall be handled in accordance with the relevant laws of China concerning foreign-invested enterprises. Zhengzhou Zhenglin shall be responsible for completing the relevant legal procedures, and the expenses incurred shall be borne by Zhengzhou Zhenglin. 5. If, due to policy or legal obstacles or reasons attributable to Zhengzhou Zhenglin, the legal procedures for the debt-to-equity conversion cannot be completed within 180 days, Zhengzhou Zhenglin undertakes to repay the entire debt owed to Lin Bojun in cash or by offset with all its tangible assets within 30 days after the expiration of that period. 6. This mediation agreement shall take effect after being judicially confirmed by the people's court.

The Henan High People's Court held that Lin Bojun is a citizen of the State of California, the United States of America. The lawsuit filed in the people's court of the People's Republic of China due to a debt dispute is a foreign-related civil and commercial case accepted by the people's court of the People's Republic of China and shall be governed by the procedural laws of the People's Republic of China. The acceptance of this case by this court, as the people's court where the defendant is domiciled, complies with the special provisions on foreign-related civil procedure in the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the jurisdiction over foreign-related civil and commercial cases. Since both parties agreed to apply the laws of the People's Republic of China, the substantive laws of the People's Republic of China shall be the governing law for this case. Upon review, the above agreement voluntarily reached by both parties does not violate the laws of the People's Republic of China, and this court confirms it. The court issued the Civil Mediation Document (2008) Yu Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 2 based on the above mediation agreement, which was signed and received by both parties.

Lanzhou Zhenglin, dissatisfied with the original mediation document, filed an application for retrial with this Court, requesting: 1. to revoke the Civil Mediation Document (2008) Yu Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 2 issued by the Henan High People's Court in accordance with the law; 2. to add Lanzhou Zhenglin to participate in the lawsuit and dismiss Lin Bojun's claims in accordance with the law. The main reasons are as follows:

I. Important facts of this case. Lanzhou Zhenglin is a wholly Taiwan-invested enterprise, established in 1991 by eight Taiwanese investors including Lin Ken and Guo Yaopeng. On August 23, 2007, all shareholders of the company held a board meeting and formed a "Board Resolution" deciding: "The term of office of Lin Ken has expired. By vote of all shareholders, it is decided to appoint Director Guo Yaopeng as Chairman." Zhengzhou Zhenglin was jointly invested and established by seven Taiwanese investors (including members of both the Guo Yaopeng and Lin Ken families) in January 2006, with Lin Ken as the legal representative. On July 31, 2008, Lin Ken (representing Lanzhou Zhenglin), Jiang Chongxu (Lin Ken's cousin, representing Zhengzhou Zhenglin), and Lin Bojun (Lin Ken's elder sister, a citizen of the State of California, the United States of America), falsely using the name of the applicant and using the applicant's company seal that Lin Ken had not returned, signed the so-called tripartite "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement". The "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement" stipulated that the applicant's creditor rights of RMB 99,406,235.82 against the respondent Zhengzhou Zhenglin would be transferred in their entirety to Lin Bojun without consideration; the applicant would no longer hold any creditor rights against Zhengzhou Zhenglin; and the full assets of Zhengzhou Zhenglin would provide security to Lin Bojun. If Zhengzhou Zhenglin failed to repay within 30 days, Lin Bojun had the right to offset the debt with all assets of Zhengzhou Zhenglin provided as security, or to convert all of Lin Bojun's debt into equity in Zhengzhou Zhenglin, with Lin Bojun becoming a shareholder of Zhengzhou Zhenglin and enjoying shareholder rights. Lin Bojun filed a lawsuit with the Henan High People's Court on October 6, 2008. After accepting the case, the Henan High People's Court served the copy of the complaint and the notice of response to Zhengzhou Zhenglin on November 3, 2008. On November 14, without obtaining the consent of other shareholders of Zhengzhou Zhenglin and without a board resolution, the two agents of Zhengzhou Zhenglin and Lin Bojun reached the so-called mediation agreement under the auspices of the Henan High People's Court. On the same day, this mediation agreement was confirmed by the Civil Mediation Document (2008) Yu Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 2. The content of this civil mediation document is essentially identical to the content of the "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement".

II. The Civil Mediation Document (2008) Yu Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 2 violates facts and the law and should be revoked in accordance with the law.

1. The "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement" signed by Zhengzhou Zhenglin and Lin Bojun on July 31, 2008, is forged and invalid. Lanzhou Zhenglin never made a decision to transfer creditor rights of RMB 99,406,235.82 to Lin Bojun, and certainly never made a decision to transfer them without consideration. Lanzhou Zhenglin and its legal representative Guo Yaopeng never authorized Lin Ken or anyone else to sign the so-called tripartite "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement". At the time of signing the tripartite "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement", i.e., July 31, 2008, Lin Ken was no longer the Chairman of Lanzhou Zhenglin and had no authority to exercise rights externally on behalf of Lanzhou Zhenglin, nor did he have the authority to decide on major matters such as the assignment of creditor's rights.

2. Lin Ken, his elder sister Lin Bojun, and his cousin Jiang Chongxu maliciously colluded to sign the so-called tripartite "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement", covering an illegal purpose with a lawful form, misappropriating the property of Lanzhou Zhenglin, and seriously infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of the applicant.

3. When presiding over the mediation, the Henan High People's Court disregarded Lin Bojun's first claim to confirm the lawfulness and validity of the tripartite "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement", made no review of whether the tripartite "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement" was lawful and valid, and ultimately caused the invalid "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement" to be confirmed by the court's mediation document.

This Court holds: As the plaintiff in the original trial, Lin Bojun raised two claims: first, to confirm that the "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement" signed by Zhengzhou Zhenglin, Lanzhou Zhenglin, and Lin Bojun is lawful and valid; second, to order the original defendant Zhengzhou Zhenglin to immediately repay Lin Bojun RMB 99,406,235.82 in accordance with the "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement". In the original trial, the mediation agreement reached between Lin Bojun and Zhengzhou Zhenglin did not address the first claim, but only formed a consensus on the second claim. Since Lanzhou Zhenglin did not participate in this lawsuit and did not sign or seal the mediation agreement, regardless of the motive or intent of Lin Bojun and Zhengzhou Zhenglin in reaching the mediation agreement, and regardless of whether they reached the mediation agreement based on the "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement", it is not binding on Lanzhou Zhenglin. The mediation document issued by the original court naturally does not have legal effect against Lanzhou Zhenglin. If Zhengzhou Zhenglin indeed owes a debt to Lanzhou Zhenglin, Zhengzhou Zhenglin cannot use this mediation document as a basis to exempt itself from the debt owed to Lanzhou Zhenglin, nor can it use this mediation document as a basis for Lanzhou Zhenglin's assignment of creditor's rights to Lin Bojun. Therefore, this mediation document objectively cannot have the consequence of harming Lanzhou Zhenglin's creditor rights. If Lanzhou Zhenglin believes it holds creditor rights against Zhengzhou Zhenglin, it may resolve the matter by filing a separate lawsuit. As to whether there was malicious collusion in the "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement" or whether it covered an illegal purpose with a lawful form, these issues can be adjudicated and resolved in that separate lawsuit. Furthermore, since the original mediation document in this case did not confirm the validity of the "Creditor's Rights Assignment Agreement", it may be deemed that Lin Bojun abandoned the first claim. The second claim is unrelated to Lanzhou Zhenglin, and whether or not Lanzhou Zhenglin participates in the lawsuit does not affect its litigation rights or civil rights.

In summary, Lanzhou Zhenglin, as an outsider to the original mediation document, can resolve its creditor-debtor relationship with Zhengzhou Zhenglin by filing a separate lawsuit. Since the original mediation document did not determine or dispose of the creditor-debtor relationship between Lanzhou Zhenglin and Zhengzhou Zhenglin, Lanzhou Zhenglin's application for retrial of the original mediation document does not satisfy the circumstances under which an outsider may initiate retrial proceedings as provided in Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 5 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China in the Trial Supervision Procedure. Pursuant to Article 181, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court rules as follows:

The retrial application of Lanzhou Zhenglin Agricultural & Food Co., Ltd. is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Lu Xiaolong
Judge: Xi Xiangyang
Acting Judge: Yang Honglei

December 22, 2010

Clerk: Xu Yinglin

[Profile of the Presiding Judge]

Lu Xiaolong, Senior Judge: born in 1965, Doctor of Laws. Appointed as judge of the Supreme People's Court in 1999.
